=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml: `claude-pr-catch-all` job env block (lines ~322-336) and scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py:sweep() | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new `claude-pr-catch-all` sweep job and `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py` never read `CLAUDE_FIXER_ENABLED`. The job env passes `CLAUDE_PR_SWEEP_MIN_AGE_HOURS`, `CLAUDE_FIX_CLAIM_LEASE_HOURS`, `CLAUDE_FIX_HAND_BACK_CAP`, etc., but not `CLAUDE_FIXER_ENABLED`, and `sweep()` has no check for it. So when an operator sets `vars.CLAUDE_FIXER_ENABLED=false` (documented in the CLAUDE.md §26.H text added by this same PR as turning Claude-fixer mode off, and in the changelog as "sends every Claude PR back to the GPT path"), the review workflow's gate correctly routes `claude/*` PRs to the GPT editor/resolver, but the hourly sweep still starts fresh Opus 5.5 `/fix-claude-pr` sessions for any `claude/*` PR whose fix has been due ≥2h with no live claim. For consumer repos the gap is structural: the sweep runs in coding-workflows and cannot read a consumer's per-repo `CLAUDE_FIXER_ENABLED` var at all.
  WHY: Set `CLAUDE_FIXER_ENABLED=false`. A `claude/*` PR that the GPT path also fails to clear (e.g. it reaches `ai:review-blocked` after `MAX_AUTOFIX_ITERATIONS`, or the resolver escalates) sits with a block label and no active run. The sweep sees `state: blocked` → `done: true`, fires the dispatcher routine, and a Claude session claims the head and pushes a `[claude-autofix]`/`[claude-intervention]` commit — exactly what the operator disabled. The only way to stop the sweep is to remove `CLAUDE_ISSUE_ROUTINE_TOKEN`, which is an undocumented separate kill switch.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
